decisions.decision: Epic 7 manual AI Intelligence Strip refresh = Pro-only (cost control)
decisions.why: MVP cost discipline. Manual refresh is spammable (each click = AI call). Auto-regen on session is already bounded by free session limits (~$0.05 lifetime per Free user, negligible). Hiding manual refresh from Free eliminates spam risk while still showing strip value AND creates upgrade pressure (matches Story 6.5 Pro-gating pattern).

decisions.decision: Epic 7 migration numbering = ship-order at dev-time, not story-number
decisions.why: Epic 7 stories ship out of numeric order (7.1 → 7.4 → 7.2 → 7.7 → 7.6 → 7.5 → 7.3). Several stories add columns to same tables (clients, sessions). Postgres migrations apply in fixed sequence — numbering by story would create out-of-order chaos. All migrations written idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) for safety.

decisions.decision: Story 7.5 email provider = nodemailer/Gmail, NOT Resend
decisions.why: Story 5.1 spec called for Resend; actual production code uses nodemailer + Gmail (apps/web/src/lib/mail.ts). Story 5.8 (transactional emails) was DROPPED so Resend was never wired. Epic 7 spec's "Resend already configured" is incorrect. Reusing existing nodemailer pattern avoids adding a new vendor/cost during MVP launch.

decisions.decision: Story 7.6 action_items uses existing 'assignee' column, NOT new 'assignee_type'
decisions.why: Epic 7 spec said add 'assignee_type'. Existing migration 015 already created 'assignee TEXT CHECK (assignee IN coach, client)'. Adding a parallel column = duplication + confusion. Same for 'completed BOOLEAN' (existing) vs proposed 'status' field. Decision: extend existing CHECK to allow 'unknown'; keep 'completed' BOOLEAN as-is. No rename.

decisions.decision: Story 7.3 deletes old Story 1.8 onboarding entirely (no parallel old/new flow)
decisions.why: apps/web/src/app/onboarding/page.tsx + components/onboarding/* directory were built for Story 1.8 (pre-pivot, video conferencing era). Epic 7 superseded that entirely. Keeping both = dead code + confusion + maintenance burden. Cleanest: delete during 7.3, rebuild under same /onboarding route. Story 5.5 (old 5-step onboarding spec) was also already declared superseded.

decisions.decision: Demo client Alex Rivera brief = hand-written static content, not per-signup AI generation
decisions.why: Path B onboarding aha moment depends on Alex's brief feeling real. Generating per-signup adds AI cost ($0.01/signup brief gen) and quality variance. Hand-written content baked into demo-client-data.ts + seeded into coach_briefs table on signup. Real Story 6.4 component renders it. Zero per-signup AI cost; higher content quality; deterministic.

decisions.decision: Gladia diarized transcript replaces 6.2b streaming transcript as the final version
decisions.why: Recall's live streaming transcript (6.2b) gives in-meeting immediacy but weak diarization. Gladia re-transcribes the recording post-meeting with 2-3x fewer speaker errors. The diarized transcript overwrites sessions.transcript_text and the AI summary is regenerated on it.

decisions.decision: Bot sessions summarized once by the Gladia pipeline; finalize-streaming skips eager summary
decisions.why: Bot sessions are summarized by the Gladia path on the diarized transcript. Letting finalize-streaming also summarize on

decisions.decision: Raw bot audio not actively deleted; rely on Recall's 7-day GC, no copy to our storage
decisions.why: Story 6.2c recording playback depends on the Recall recording existing. Actively deleting it after Gladia transcription would break playback. Copying audio to our own storage adds cost. Recall's 7-day garbage collection satisfies privacy (auto-purged) while keeping playback available for the week after a meeting.
